ALPHA USER GUIDE

01 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Start here

Bursara brings student fees, bills, receipts and unpaid balances into one workspace. This guide covers the working alpha.

How to use it

  1. Open https://app.bursara.com in your browser. Use the login supplied by your institution or the demonstration access shared separately.
  2. Start with Courses & units, then enrol a student. A course is the full programme; a unit is a priced part of that programme.
  3. Create a bill, receive a payment and open the resulting receipt. Return to the student account to see the remaining balance.
  4. Use About this screen whenever you need a reminder. This guide follows the same button and field names as the application.

What to expect

The protected example school is BURARA CHILRENS ACADEMY. It uses fictional records and is shared with other testers. Never enter real student details, real payments or confidential information into the alpha demonstration.

This is an evaluation release. Posted examples can be corrected through credits or refunds, but alpha records may also be reset during development. Classroom allocation, attendance and timetables are outside the current release.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd3 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

02 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Understand the money words

A few everyday terms make the rest of the screens easier to follow.

How to use it

  1. A bill or invoice says what a student or their responsible party owes. It can cover the whole year even when payment will come in smaller parts.
  2. A receipt acknowledges money already received. Recording a bill alone does not mean the school has received money.
  3. An allocation applies a received payment to a particular bill. The bill then shows a lower outstanding balance.
  4. An instalment is one scheduled amount and due date within a bill. Outstanding includes every unpaid amount; overdue includes only amounts whose due dates have passed.
  5. Unapplied credit is money received for a student that has not yet been used against a bill. A fee credit reduces a charge; a refund returns unused money.

What to expect

Example: a MUR 120,000 annual bill paid in twelve monthly instalments still starts as one MUR 120,000 bill. A MUR 25,000 allocated payment leaves MUR 95,000 outstanding. The overdue amount depends on the instalment dates and the selected balance date.

A bill, receipt and fee credit are different financial records even when an institution chooses a combined invoice/receipt workflow.

03 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Sign in and sign out

Sign in to reach the workspace your administrator has assigned to you.

How to use it

  1. If you have registered a passkey, select Sign in with passkey (4) and follow your device’s verification prompt. Otherwise enter Email address (1) and Password (2), then select Sign in (3).
  2. If the password method opens Verify your sign-in, enter the current code from your authenticator app or one unused recovery code. Select Verify and sign in.
  3. Institution users arrive at their own institution. Platform staff arrive at Client institutions. A verified passkey signs you in without a separate authenticator-code step.
  4. If the email or password is incorrect, check the spelling and try again. After five failed attempts for the same account and connection, wait the number of seconds shown.
  5. When finished, select Sign out at the bottom of the navigation menu. On a shared computer, close the browser after signing out.

What to expect

Your institution administrator creates ordinary user accounts and can set a new password through Users & permissions. A password reset does not remove an enabled authenticator. This alpha does not provide a self-service forgotten-password screen.

The shared demonstration login is protected. Its password cannot be changed and it cannot enrol passkeys or time-based one-time passwords. Private platform staff credentials are never included in this guide.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd5 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

04 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Passkeys, verification and recovery

Sign-in security protects your own login. These options are available to institution users and platform staff; the shared demonstration login stays locked.

How to use it

  1. Open Sign-in security. To add a passkey, enter a Passkey name, such as Office laptop, and select Add a passkey.
  2. A change opens Confirm it’s you. Enter Current password, plus an Authenticator or recovery code if your authenticator is already enabled. Select Continue, then follow any device prompt.
  3. To enable verification codes, select Set up authenticator app. After confirming your identity, scan the displayed QR code with your authenticator app or enter its setup key privately.
  4. Enter Code from your authenticator app and select Enable authenticator. Password sign-in will now require your app’s current code or an unused recovery code.
  5. Save all eight codes from Save your recovery codes in a private place you can reach if your phone is lost. Use the copy or download action, then select I’ve saved these codes.
  6. Each recovery code works once. Replace recovery codes creates a new set and invalidates the old set. Save the replacement codes before closing the panel.
  7. A registered passkey is an alternative sign-in method: select Sign in with passkey and verify on your device. It does not ask for a separate authenticator code.
  8. To retire a passkey, use Remove beside its name. To disable app verification, select Turn off authenticator. Confirm your identity as prompted and keep another working way to sign in.

What to expect

Keep setup keys and recovery codes private. If you cannot use your passkey, authenticator or recovery codes, contact your institution administrator or Bursara support for account recovery.

The demonstration login cannot register passkeys or enable an authenticator. Changing another user’s password in Users & permissions does not remove their extra sign-in protection.

05 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Find your way around

The left menu groups the daily work. The floating help control explains the screen you are viewing.

How to use it

  1. Use Students (1) for learners and their individual accounts. Use Courses & units for programmes and their fees.
  2. Use Billing (2) for posted charges and Payments (3) for received money and receipts.
  3. Use Debtors (4) to follow unpaid fees. Reports contains currency summaries, the financial control journal and the balance export.
  4. Select About this screen at the lower right. Read the explanation, then select the same control again to close it.
  5. Open Sign-in security to protect your own login. If another menu item or action is missing, ask your administrator whether your user has the relevant permission.

What to expect

Opening an invoice, receipt or student account does not change its figures. Posting a bill, receiving money, applying credit, issuing a credit or recording a refund does change the financial records.

Tables use a ledger layout. Move the pointer over a row to highlight it, then select the document number, student name or small open arrow.

06 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Read the overview

The overview gives a quick account position for one currency and one date.

How to use it

  1. Choose Balance date (2). The figures use financial records up to that date, so changing it lets you review an earlier position.
  2. Choose Display currency (3). Each currency has its own figures; selecting USD does not convert every MUR transaction into dollars.
  3. Read the four totals (1): Fees billed, Payments received, Outstanding and Overdue.
  4. Look at unapplied student credit below the totals. This is received money still available to apply to a student's bills.
  5. Open a document in Recent bills or Recent collections, or use Create bill and Receive payment when your permissions allow them.

What to expect

Outstanding and overdue answer different questions. A future instalment is outstanding but is not overdue. An instalment due today becomes overdue only after that day has passed.

The overview is a starting point. Open the relevant bill, student account or report to understand a particular figure.

07 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Create a course

A course is the complete programme, such as High School or BSc Biomedical Sciences.

How to use it

  1. Open Courses & units and select New course.
  2. Enter Course name (1) in language that school staff will recognise.
  3. Enter a short Code (2), such as HS. Codes must be unique within your institution.
  4. Optionally enter a Description, then select Create course (3).
  5. Add the priced units next. Creating the course by itself does not bill any student.

What to expect

For a school that bills by year, create one High School course and units such as Year 1, Year 2, Year 3 and Year 4. For a university programme, use the programme as the course and the subjects or modules as units.

The alpha creates courses and units but does not provide a separate edit or delete workflow for them. Review names, codes and prices before saving.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd9 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

08 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Set a fixed unit fee

Use a fixed fee when the price applies to the entire unit, such as one school year.

How to use it

  1. In Courses & units, select Add unit. Choose its Course (1).
  2. Enter Unit name and a unique Code. For example, use Year 1 and Y1.
  3. Enter Price (2) and choose Currency. Enter amounts as numbers without currency symbols or thousands separators.
  4. Choose Fixed unit fee in Price basis (3). For a whole-year fee, leave Credits / weight as 1.
  5. Select Save unit. The unit will appear under its course and can be selected when enrolling a student.

What to expect

Example: Year 1 has a fixed price of MUR 120,000. Billing a quantity of 1 produces MUR 120,000 before any line discount or tax.

The currency belongs to the unit. Units using different currencies need separate bills. Entering the unit does not automatically enrol students or create bills.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd10 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

09 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Set a fee per credit

Use a per-credit fee when the unit charge depends on its credit weight.

How to use it

  1. Select Add unit and choose the programme in Course.
  2. Enter the unit name and code, such as Cell Biology and BIO101.
  3. Enter the price for one credit in Price (1), then choose Currency (2).
  4. Choose Per credit in Price basis (3). Enter the number of credits in Credits / weight (4).
  5. Select Save unit. When this enrolled unit is selected on a bill, Bursara fills the quantity with its credit weight.

What to expect

Example: a unit with a USD 250 price per credit and a weight of 3 credits gives a USD 750 fee before discount or tax.

The posted bill uses the quantity and unit price shown on its fee line. Check them before posting. Unit prices support up to five decimal places and credit weights up to three; the final amount is rounded to the currency's normal precision.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd11 / 41

10 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Enrol a student

Enrolment connects a learner, the party responsible for paying and the units that may be billed.

How to use it

  1. Open Students and select Enrol student. Enter Student name (1) and a unique Student reference.
  2. Enter the Debtor / billing contact (2): the person or organisation responsible for the fees. Choose Parent / guardian, Student or Sponsor / employer under Responsible party.
  3. Optionally enter a student email, contact phone and billing address. Use fictional details while testing the alpha.
  4. Choose Course (3). Tick the Billable units (4) in which the student is enrolled.
  5. Select Enrol student. Bursara opens the Student account. Check the learner, programme and billing contact.

What to expect

Units must belong to the chosen course. A priced unit cannot be billed to a student until that student is enrolled in it. A custom fee can also be entered directly on a bill.

The student reference distinguishes learners with similar names. The alpha does not yet include editing an existing enrolment, promotions between school years, attendance or a student timetable.

11 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Use a student account

The student account brings one learner's bills and receipts together.

How to use it

  1. Open Students, search by name, reference or debtor, and select the student name or open arrow.
  2. Check the learner and billing-contact details (3). These identify the account being reviewed.
  3. Read the outstanding amount and unapplied credit for each currency. Different currencies stay separate.
  4. Use the Fee register to open a bill. Use the Receipt register to open a receipt.
  5. Select Create bill (2), Receive payment or Print statement (1) as needed. Your permissions determine which actions are available.

What to expect

The student account is useful when a parent or sponsor asks what remains to be paid. Open the individual bill to see its monthly due dates and exactly how payments have been applied.

Unapplied credit is shown separately from outstanding fees. It does not settle a bill until you explicitly apply it.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd13 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

12 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Choose the billing workflow

Choose how the charge and the collection should be recorded before posting.

How to use it

  1. Open Billing and select Create bill. Select the correct Student (1).
  2. Choose Bill first, collect later in Billing workflow (2) when you want an invoice now and will receive money separately.
  3. Choose Assessed fees with instalments when you want a fee assessment and a scheduled series of due amounts. This also starts with an unpaid bill.
  4. Choose Receive full payment and issue only when the entire bill has already been paid. This creates the bill and its full payment together.
  5. For a partial payment, use Bill first, collect later, post the bill, then use Receive payment for the part received.

What to expect

Receive full payment and issue requires both permission to create invoices and permission to receive payments. It is not a method for promising a future payment.

Bill first and assessed fees both support monthly instalments. The workflow describes your process; it does not automatically collect money from a bank or card.

13 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Create an annual school bill

Bill the whole school year once and then collect the money over time.

How to use it

  1. Select the student and choose Bill first, collect later. Enter the Issue date and a clear Service period, such as Academic year 2027.
  2. Under Fee lines, choose the student's school year in Enrolled unit (1). Bursara fills Description, Quantity / credits and Unit price (2).
  3. Confirm Currency. If it differs from the institution's functional currency, enter the conversion rate shown by the rate field.
  4. Check Line discount and Tax %. These are line amounts and percentages, not changes to a previously posted invoice.
  5. Continue to First due date and Monthly instalments. Review every line before selecting Post bill.

What to expect

A fixed annual fee of MUR 120,000 with quantity 1 is one annual charge. Choosing twelve instalments changes the payment schedule, not the total fee.

Use Add line for another charge and the remove icon to remove a line before posting. Posted money records cannot be edited in place.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd15 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

14 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Set monthly instalments

The schedule says when parts of a bill fall due. It does not create extra invoices or extra fees.

How to use it

  1. In Create a bill, enter the First due date (1). It must be on or after the bill's Issue date.
  2. Choose the number of Monthly instalments (2). Choose One payment due when the full bill is due on one date.
  3. Add any Notes that should appear with the bill.
  4. Select Post bill (3). On the invoice, review Payment schedule and confirm every scheduled amount and date.
  5. Use Receive payment later when the student pays. Bursara applies a payment to the earliest unpaid instalments first.

What to expect

Example: MUR 120,000 over twelve instalments gives MUR 10,000 each. If cents cannot divide evenly, Bursara distributes the small remainder so that the instalments add up to the exact bill total.

Monthly dates retain the chosen day where possible. A schedule starting on 31 January uses 28 February, or 29 February in a leap year, and then 31 March. Automatic repeat invoice generation is not part of this alpha.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd16 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

15 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Bill university units

Use one or more enrolled units instead of a whole-year school fee.

How to use it

  1. Create a bill and select the university student. Check the Service period, such as Semester 1 / 2027.
  2. Choose a subject under Enrolled unit. A per-credit unit fills Quantity / credits (3) with the credit weight and Unit price (4) with the price for one credit.
  3. Check Currency (1). Enter the requested Rate (2) when that currency differs from the institution's functional currency.
  4. Use Add line for another unit in the same currency. Create a separate bill for a unit with a different currency.
  5. Choose the due schedule, review the fee lines and select Post bill.

What to expect

Example: 3 credits at USD 250 per credit gives a USD 750 line. A fixed USD 400 laboratory unit can be added as a second line with quantity 1.

The bill captures its own prices and conversion rate. Changing a unit in a future release will not mean rewriting already posted financial records.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd17 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

16 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Receive full payment and issue together

Use this workflow when the entire fee is paid at the time you issue the document.

How to use it

  1. Create the bill and choose Receive full payment and issue in Billing workflow.
  2. Complete the student, dates, service period, currency and fee lines as for any bill.
  3. Choose the Payment method (2). Enter a Payment reference if you have a bank, card or other confirmation reference.
  4. Check that the full charge has really been received. Select Receive and issue document (3).
  5. Open the resulting invoice/receipt. Confirm that Outstanding is zero and that its recorded payment can be opened.

What to expect

This makes one bill and one receipt for the full amount. Repeated clicks or a repeated submission should not create a second set of financial records.

For a part payment, post an ordinary bill and receive that part separately. A payment method records how money arrived; Bursara does not itself charge a card or initiate a bank transfer.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd18 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

17 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Read a posted invoice

The posted invoice is the record of the charge, its payments and its unpaid balance.

How to use it

  1. Open Billing, find the bill and select its number. Use the search and status filter if needed.
  2. Check the invoice number, issue date and status (1). Then check the institution, billing contact, student and service period.
  3. Review the lines: description, quantity, unit price, discount, tax and amount.
  4. Read Total fees, Payments applied, Credits and Outstanding in the summary (2). Review Payment schedule below it.
  5. Use Receive payment to collect against this bill. Use Credit outstanding fees only when you need to reduce an unpaid charge.

What to expect

Outstanding means the total still unpaid, including future instalments. The invoice can be outstanding, part paid or settled. Settled means its outstanding balance is zero.

Posted bills cannot be silently changed. Fee credits create separate correction records. Bills with fiscal documents require their local e-invoicing correction workflow, which is outside the alpha fiscal module.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd19 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

18 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Record a partial payment

Record only the money actually received, then apply it to the student's bill.

How to use it

  1. Open an unpaid invoice and select Receive payment. The student and bill are preselected.
  2. Enter the Amount received (1). If MUR 25,000 arrived, enter 25000 even when the full bill is MUR 120,000.
  3. Check Received date (2), Method (3), Payer and Reference. Use a bank transfer only after it is confirmed, or Cleared cheque only after it has cleared.
  4. In Allocate to bills, leave the correct bill selected and enter the portion to apply in Apply (MUR).
  5. Select Receive and issue receipt. Open the bill again and check its new Outstanding amount.

What to expect

Example: applying MUR 25,000 to a MUR 120,000 bill leaves MUR 95,000 outstanding. The payment pays the earliest unpaid instalments first.

The amount applied cannot exceed the bill balance or the money available from the payment. An allocated payment cannot be dated before its bill.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd20 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

19 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Allocate one payment to bills

An allocation tells Bursara which unpaid charge the received money should settle.

How to use it

  1. Open Payments and select Receive payment. Choose the student and fill in the received amount, date, currency and method.
  2. Under Allocate to bills, tick each bill that this payment should help settle.
  3. Enter the amount to apply for each selected bill. The total used from the payment must not exceed Amount received.
  4. Leave a bill unticked when this payment is not intended for it. Any unused received money remains unapplied student credit.
  5. Select Receive and issue receipt. Review Applied to fees on the receipt and follow an invoice link to check its balance.

What to expect

A payment can be applied to several bills for the same student. It cannot be applied to another student's bill or to another institution.

For one currency, the applied bill amount and the amount used from the payment are the same. For different currencies, you must enter both sides, as explained in the next procedure.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd21 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

20 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Receive a payment in another currency

Record the currency received and the amount of the bill that it settles as two separate amounts.

How to use it

  1. Open Receive a payment and choose the payment Currency. Enter Amount received in that currency.
  2. Enter the Rate requested by the form (1). Read the label carefully: Rate: 1 USD in MUR means how many MUR equal one USD.
  3. Tick the bill being paid. Enter Apply (MUR) (2) as the amount to remove from the MUR bill.
  4. Enter Uses (USD) (3) as the part of the USD payment used for that allocation.
  5. Check both amounts and the rate, then select Receive and issue receipt. Review the currencies shown in Applied to fees.

What to expect

Example: the school receives USD 100 and agrees that this settles MUR 4,600 of a bill. Enter 100 received, 4600 in Apply (MUR), 100 in Uses (USD), and the appropriate rate of 46.

Bursara does not fetch exchange rates automatically. Your institution must supply the correct rate and agreed settlement amounts. MUR, USD and most supported currencies use two decimal places; JPY uses none and KWD uses three.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd22 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

21 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Record an advance payment

Keep money received before it is assigned to a bill as unapplied student credit.

How to use it

  1. Open Payments and select Receive payment. Select the correct Student and Payer.
  2. Enter Amount received, Currency, Received date, Method and any Reference.
  3. Under Allocate to bills, leave every bill unticked (2). If the student has no unpaid bills, the form explains that the money will be held as credit.
  4. Select Receive and issue receipt (3). Review Unapplied credit on the receipt.
  5. Keep the receipt reference. Later, open it to apply available credit to a bill or refund unused money.

What to expect

An advance is still a receipt because money has arrived. It does not reduce any invoice until you apply it.

Recording an advance separately is the correct approach when the received date is earlier than the bill issue date. Do not create a false earlier bill just to make the allocation fit.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd23 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

22 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Apply existing student credit

Use an earlier unapplied payment against an outstanding bill without recording the money twice.

How to use it

  1. Open the original receipt from Payments or the student's Receipt register.
  2. If credit remains and a same-currency bill is unpaid, select Apply student credit.
  3. Choose the Outstanding invoice (1). Enter Apply amount (MUR), or the currency shown (2).
  4. Enter Allocation date (3). It cannot be earlier than the original payment, the bill or a refund already recorded against that payment.
  5. Select Apply credit to bill (4). Check that the receipt's unapplied credit and the bill's outstanding amount both decrease.

What to expect

This is an application of money already received. Do not use Receive payment again for the same money.

The alpha applies existing credit to bills in the same currency and for the same student. If the action is absent, check the receipt's available credit, the student's unpaid bills and your permission to receive payments.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd24 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

23 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Refund unused credit

Record money returned from the part of a payment that has not been applied to bills.

How to use it

  1. Open the receipt and check its Unapplied credit. Select Refund unused credit.
  2. Enter the refund Amount in the currency shown (1). It cannot exceed the available unapplied credit.
  3. Enter Date. The refund cannot predate the original payment.
  4. Enter a clear Reason (2), then select Record refund (3).
  5. Confirm that Refunded increases and Unapplied credit decreases on the receipt. Keep the real-world payment reference in your own process as needed.

What to expect

This records a refund that your institution has arranged. It does not send money to a bank or card.

Only unused credit can be refunded in this alpha. Returning money that has already been applied to a bill needs a fuller reversal workflow and is not supported here. Do not record a negative payment to work around that limit.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd25 / 41
ALPHA USER GUIDE

24 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Reduce an outstanding fee

A fee credit reduces a charge that remains unpaid, for example an approved scholarship adjustment.

How to use it

  1. Open the invoice and select Credit outstanding fees. The action requires credit/refund permission.
  2. Enter Amount in the invoice currency (1). It cannot exceed the current outstanding balance.
  3. Enter Date (2), on or after the bill issue date and any payment already applied to the bill.
  4. Enter a clear Reason (3), then select Record credit (4).
  5. Check the invoice's Credits and Outstanding figures. The original charge remains visible and the credit appears as a separate record.

What to expect

A fee credit does not return cash. To record money returned from an unused advance, use Refund unused credit on its receipt.

Credit is applied to the latest unpaid scheduled amounts first. If the bill has a fiscal document, Bursara blocks this core credit action because the local e-invoicing module must handle the fiscal correction. Fiscal credit notes are not implemented in this alpha.

25 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Read and print a receipt

The receipt shows money received, the bills paid from it and any money still unused.

How to use it

  1. Open Payments and select a receipt number. Check the payer, student, received date, method and reference.
  2. Read Amount received (1). Under Applied to fees, follow an invoice number to inspect its charge and outstanding balance.
  3. Check Refunded and Unapplied credit (2). These explain why some of the received amount may no longer be available to allocate.
  4. Select Print / PDF. In your browser's print window, choose a printer or Save as PDF.
  5. Check the print preview before saving or printing. The navigation and action buttons are left out of the printed document.

What to expect

Demonstration documents are marked as testing documents. They must not be used as real tax invoices or real payment acknowledgements.

An institution may use the combined invoice/receipt workflow when charging and collecting together. The receipt register still records the money received.

26 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Print a student statement

Use a statement to review one student's charges and receipts together.

How to use it

  1. Open Students and select the learner. Confirm the correct name and reference.
  2. Review outstanding fees and unapplied credit for each currency, then review the Fee register and Receipt register.
  3. Select Print statement (1). Choose your printer or Save as PDF in the browser print window.
  4. Check the preview and page breaks. Save or print the statement using your institution's usual document-sharing process.

What to expect

The statement reflects the current student account. It is not a new invoice or a new receipt and does not change the balance.

To explain a particular instalment or payment, open the related invoice or receipt as well. Use Debtors or Reports with Balance date when you need an institution-wide position at an earlier date.

27 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Follow outstanding and overdue fees

Debtors helps staff follow up the fees that remain unpaid.

How to use it

  1. Open Debtors. Select Balance date (1) to choose the date of the position you want to inspect.
  2. Choose Display currency (2). Read Outstanding fees and Overdue instalments (3).
  3. Use Search records to find a student, debtor or invoice. The table shows open bills in the selected currency.
  4. Open a bill to inspect its Payment schedule and Outstanding amount.
  5. If money has arrived, use Receive payment. If an approved unpaid charge must be reduced, use Credit outstanding fees.

What to expect

Outstanding includes unpaid future instalments. Overdue includes scheduled amounts due before the chosen date. For example, a MUR 95,000 balance is not necessarily MUR 95,000 overdue.

This alpha provides the open-balance view. Automatic reminder emails, collection campaigns and a separate collection-case workflow are not included. Follow your institution's communication process when contacting the responsible party.

28 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Review and export balances

Reports gives a currency summary and a spreadsheet-friendly list of invoice balances.

How to use it

  1. Open Reports and choose Balance date. Use the same date when comparing the report with Debtors.
  2. Read Balances by currency (2). Billed, collected, outstanding and overdue amounts are separated by currency.
  3. Select Export balances (1). Your browser downloads bursara-open-items.csv.
  4. Open the CSV in your spreadsheet application. Check the invoice, student, debtor, currency, total, paid, credit, balance and overdue columns.
  5. Keep the chosen date with the exported file so another person knows which position was reviewed.

What to expect

A CSV is a table of values, not a formatted PDF. Your spreadsheet may ask how to interpret dates, numbers or the comma separator. Collected shows the money originally received before any refunds; it is not a net-cash figure.

The alpha does not connect to an external accounting platform. Use this export for review and testing; establish the full reporting and accounting process before using Bursara for live operations.

29 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Understand the financial control journal

The journal is a supporting view for staff who need to trace the financial effect of a posting.

How to use it

  1. Open Reports and scroll to Financial control journal.
  2. Read Date and Source to identify whether an entry came from an invoice, payment, credit, refund or application of existing credit.
  3. Read Account to understand the type of movement. Movement uses the institution's functional currency.
  4. Positive amounts are debits and negative amounts are credits. The movements belonging to each posting should add to zero.
  5. Use the relevant invoice or receipt to investigate a source record. Ask the institution's finance lead if the treatment is unclear.

What to expect

This view shows the latest 100 postings. It is a financial control trail, not a complete general ledger, statutory accounts package or accounting-platform integration.

Ordinary daily users can work through bills, receipts and student accounts without reading journal entries. This screen is available only when report permission is granted.

An authorised administrator can create a login for another member of the institution's team.

How to use it

Set the right permissions

Bursara checks these permissions whenever someone tries an action.

How to use it

  1. Open Users & permissions. Select Edit permissions for an ordinary user.
  2. Tick Manage students for enrolment and Manage courses and fees for creating programmes and their priced units.
  3. Tick Create invoices for posting bills and Receive payments for recording collections or applying existing credit. Receive full payment and issue needs both rights.
  4. Tick Issue credits and refunds only for users authorised to make financial corrections. Use View and export reports, Manage fiscal modules and Manage institution settings where needed.
  5. Grant Manage institution users only to trusted administrators. Select Save user and rights after reviewing the checkboxes.

What to expect

A permission is a right to perform an action, not a change of institution. Removing an action right can remove its button or make a direct request to it fail.

An explicit empty checkbox selection grants none of these action rights. Your account cannot remove its own user-management access through this form. To change a non-demo user’s password, enter a new password; leave it blank to keep the existing one. This does not disable that user’s authenticator or remove their passkeys.

36 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Prepare and review a sandbox fiscal document

Preparing a fiscal document and submitting it are separate actions in this alpha.

How to use it

  1. With EBS sandbox enabled, use Prepare a sandbox document in Modules. Select the Invoice. In payment mode, also select its allocated Payment.
  2. Select Prepare sandbox document. The new row appears in Fiscal register with a prepared status.
  3. Select Review to inspect the document and any provider result. Check the institution, reference, amount, currency and event before submission.
  4. Only an authorised tester with valid sandbox credentials should select Submit to sandbox. This guide does not require a submission to complete the ordinary billing exercises.
  5. If a queue ID was returned, select Refresh status to check the outcome. Resolve a pending, unknown or rejected reference before preparing another document.

What to expect

The current EBS option supports undiscounted exempt or 15% service lines. When reporting a payment event, only tuition with no tax that was assigned to a bill is currently supported. A prepared document does not prove fiscal acceptance.

Accepted means the sandbox returned success. Queued means processing is pending. Unknown means the result is uncertain, for example after a connection failure. Do not resubmit an uncertain document: reconcile the original reference with EBS support. Fiscal credit notes and live fiscal submissions are outside this alpha.

38 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Solve common problems

Use the message on the screen to decide the next step. Avoid creating a second transaction to solve an uncertain first attempt.

How to use it

  1. Cannot sign in: check email and password, or use a registered passkey. If Verify your sign-in appears, use your authenticator app or an unused recovery code. After repeated failures, wait for the displayed delay. Ask the institution administrator for account help. If a verification code was just used, wait for the next code in your app.
  2. Missing button or access denied: ask an administrator to review your permission checkboxes. Client users cannot enter another institution.
  3. Unit missing from a bill: check the student's chosen course and enrolled units. Units from another course or another currency cannot be silently combined.
  4. Payment will not post: check decimal precision, positive amounts, dates and allocations. Applied amounts cannot exceed the bill or available payment.
  5. Credit or refund blocked: a fee credit cannot exceed unpaid fees; a refund cannot exceed unused student credit. Fiscal documents need their country-specific e-invoicing correction process.
  6. Unknown fiscal result: stop and reconcile the original reference. Do not submit it again just because a response was slow.

What to expect

If you are unsure whether a bill or payment was posted, first search Billing or Payments and open the student account. Check for the existing document before trying another transaction.

When reporting a problem, give the screen name, document number, steps taken, expected outcome and exact visible message. Use fictional records and remove confidential information from screenshots.

39 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Help, boundaries and quick reference

Use this final page as a short reminder and a route to support.

How to use it

  1. Institution: one school, college or learning organisation with its own isolated records.
  2. Course: the whole programme. Unit: a priced year, subject, module or other part of that programme.
  3. Debtor: the student, parent, guardian, employer or sponsor responsible for paying.
  4. Functional currency: the institution's main reporting currency. Document currency: the currency on a particular bill or receipt.
  5. Fee credit: a separate reduction of an unpaid charge. Student credit: money received but not yet applied. Refund: money returned from unused credit.
  6. For product help, contact support@streaktechnologies.com, +230 215 2998, or visit streaktechnologies.com.

What to expect
